keyVerseText: But be not thou far from me, O LORD: O my strength, haste thee to help me.
rootMeaning: The root word אֱיָל (ʼĕyâl) denotes strength and help, indicating a source of power and support. The feminine noun אֱיָלוּת (ʼĕyâlûwth) is derived from this root, emphasizing not just raw strength but also the protective and sustaining aspect of that strength. This root sense enriches the English gloss "strength" by highlighting a relational dimension—strength as an active help or defense, not merely an abstract force.
usageInScripture: The term אֱיָלוּת appears only once in Scripture, specifically in Psalms 22:19, where it is translated as "O my strength." This singular occurrence underscores its precise and poignant use to express a personal appeal to God as a source of power and aid. The consistency in translation as "strength" or "my strength" reflects its role in depicting God as a reliable protector and helper in times of distress.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding אֱיָלוּת as both strength and help deepens our appreciation of God’s character as revealed in Scripture. It portrays God not only as omnipotent but as intimately involved in providing protection and assistance to His people. This word underscores the Christian conviction that faith rests in a God who is both mighty and merciful, offering strength that sustains and rescues. Recognizing God as our אֱיָלוּת invites believers to trust in His power amid trials, affirming that true help flows from His sovereign strength.
keyVerseReflection: In Psalms 22:19, the psalmist cries out, "But be not thou far from me, O LORD: O my strength, haste thee to help me." The use of אֱיָלוּת here conveys a heartfelt plea for God’s nearness as the essential source of strength and timely aid. This word enriches the verse by portraying God not only as a distant power but as an immediate and personal helper, emphasizing the believer’s dependence on divine strength in moments of vulnerability.
